messages:
customer_jemma: Hey team — seeing a sudden spike of 429s from our production service after the auth token rotates. We traced it to retries: some retry requests are missing the Idempotency-Key header and producing duplicate side-effects. Logs + minimal details below.

mike: Sorry about that — can you share the SDK version, transport, and a tiny repro? Also any logs showing the missing header.

customer_jemma: Using redwood-python v0.14.2 with the default RequestsTransport (requests.Session). Token refresh is handled by our auth helper which swaps session headers on 401. Example log snippet: 

```
2026-02-18T14:12:22.123Z INFO request id=xyz status=401 headers={"Authorization":"Bearer expired","Idempotency-Key":"abc-123"}
2026-02-18T14:12:22.456Z INFO auth refresh: got new token
2026-02-18T14:12:22.789Z INFO retry attempt=1 id=xyz status=429 headers={"Authorization":"Bearer new","Content-Type":"application/json"}  <-- Idempotency-Key missing here
```

mike: Hmm, interesting. Are you adding the Idempotency-Key on the session (session.headers) or per-request?

customer_jemma: We were setting it on session.headers before the request b/c requests code paths in the app expect a default idempotency header. Repro script (simplified):

```
import threading
import time
import uuid
from requests import Session
from redwood import RedwoodClient

s = Session()
s.headers.update({"Authorization": "Bearer expired", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())})
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=None, transport={'session': s})  # simplified

# call that triggers auth refresh in parallel
def call():
    resp = client.requests.create("/do-side-effect", json={"x":1})
    print(resp.status_code)

# start a call which gets 401 -> refresh -> retry
call()
```

customer_jemma: After the 401, our auth helper does `session.headers = new_headers` (assignment) to replace the Authorization, but even when we changed it to `session.headers.update`, we still see the idempotency header vanish from the retry.

sophia: Thanks for the repro. I was able to reproduce locally with your pattern. Root cause looks like our retry flow reconstructs a new Request for the retry and merges session headers at retry-time, but we accidentally prefer session-level Authorization and drop headers that were present only on the PreparedRequest.headers (the Idempotency-Key in your case) when there's a modification during auth refresh. In short: a token refresh that mutates session.headers at the same time as we prepare the retry can lead to losing per-request headers.

sophia: Minimal reproducer I used (single-threaded timing to force the race):

```
# recreate: prepare, then mutate session.headers before send
from requests import Session, Request
s = Session()
s.headers.update({"Authorization": "Bearer expired", "Idempotency-Key": "keep-me"})
r = Request('POST', 'https://example.test/do', json={'x':1}, headers={})
prepped = s.prepare_request(r)
# simulate token refresh that replaces session.headers
s.headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer new"}
# our send path at retry time was re-preparing and recomputing headers
# which dropped the Idempotency-Key from prepped.headers
```

mike: Good find. Any short-term workarounds we can give the customer to avoid duplicates until a patch is out?

sophia: Yes — two practical workarounds:
1) Set the Idempotency-Key explicitly on the per-request call (e.g., client.requests.create(..., headers={"Idempotency-Key": "..."})) so the SDK uses it from the request context instead of relying on session defaults.
2) Avoid reassigning session.headers in your auth helper; use `session.headers.update({"Authorization": token})` so the session continues to carry other default headers.

sophia: We have a fix ready that ensures the retry code preserves PreparedRequest.headers (and merges session headers without clobbering per-request values) even if session.headers mutates during token refresh. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/pull/312 (targets v0.14.3). The core change is to prefer per-request/prepared headers when reconstructing retry payloads. Example patch snippet: 

```
# before: new_headers = self.session.headers.copy()
# after: new_headers = self.session.headers.copy()
#         new_headers.update(prepared_request.headers)  # ensure request-level headers win
```

rachel: deploy-bot: scheduled 0.14.3 canary to staging at 2026-02-19T02:00:00Z. Will monitor idempotency-related metrics.

customer_jemma: Thanks — testing workaround now (setting header on request). Will report back results in ~30m. Much appreciated. :pray:

mike: If you can share the request ID from a failed duplicate, we can correlate and clean up any downstream duplicates.

customer_jemma: Will do. One quick note for others: if you rely on session-level defaults for idempotency headers + have background token rotation, you might hit this edge during retries. Per-request idempotency headers are safer.

sophia: Agreed. We'll get the patch cut and published to PyPI as 0.14.3 today. I'll post the release notes and the change in this thread when done.

customer_jemma: Awesome — thanks everyone.
